results.comment: I appreciate how you made a point that not every question is legitimate or deserves an answer (8:03). I'm not obligated to provide any information on any topic unless I choose to do so OR I have a level of relationship with someone that merits revealing that information for the sake of the relationship.  Here's how I see it: If someone random on the street walked up to you and said, "Hey, I think you should give me $20 because I want it," you'd tell them to get lost. But if a trusted friend comes to you and says, "Please, I really need $20," and you know they're asking due to a legitimate need, you'll give it to them if you have it.  So if someone comes to me asking for "freebies" (that's essentially what someone is doing when they lowball you), and I haven't established a professional relationship with them, then I'm much more likely to dig my heels in and say, "Thanks, but no thanks." That's because I know that if I give in to them now, on my very first job with them, then they'll expect it from now on in every job I do for them afterwards.  It's when I've ALREADY worked with someone, and I know they're a good match and we're likely to mutually benefit from an ongoing relationship, that I'll be willing to put in an "extra" or two just because. At that point, I've established boundaries, and they know those freebies are a sign of me being glad to work with them, which makes them feel appreciated, which then makes them more likely to come back. It's a win-win.
results.comment_focus_summary: The commenter is focusing on the speaker's point that not every question deserves an answer and on boundaries around giving freebies or favors depending on relationship and legitimacy of the request.
